units.translation: In the lacunose passage Suppl. 827 the letters ἰòp [io] and ὄμ [om] are the beginnings of two verses. ἰόφ ὄμ [ioph om] is worthless, and nothing is gained by the scholiast's note, ἐπὶ ἀποπτυσμοῦ μίμημα [an imitation of spitting] (sic for μίσημα [an object of loathing] L. Dindorf in the Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 2435). ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀποπτύειν ἀπόφθεγμα [from the act of spitting he made an apophthegm] (correctly ἐπίφθεγμα [an interjection] Weilius) ἐποίησε · διὸ δεῖ τὴν ὑστέραν δασύνειν [he made; therefore the latter must be aspirated], and Eustathius p. 900, 27, where he discusses the word ὄψις [voice], ἐκ τοῦ ὄφ ἐπιφωνήματος, ὃ κατὰ πνεύματος ἀθρόαν εἰσπνοὴν ἐγγίνεται τοῖς ἀλγοῦσιν ἢ φόβον παθοῦσιν [from the interjection ὄφ, which arises from a sudden intake of breath in those suffering pain or fear].
from the act of spitting he made an apophthegm
he made; therefore the latter must be aspirated
from the interjection ὄφ, which arises from a sudden intake of breath in those suffering pain or fear
pressed down beneath the roots of Aetna
the Scythians, good law-abiding eaters of mare's-milk cheese
a monster composed of horse and cock
where see what I have noted and Thes. vol. 4 p. 629.
where the metre requires γενῦν ἱππιᾶν [horse-jawed].
neither any messenger nor any horseman
and the captured women to be led by the hair like horses
for all the horse-driving and land-treading host
and Diaixis and Arsaces, lords of horsemen
and indeed I hear the roar of equine snortings
It is read in Homer and Hesiod: see Thes. vol. 4 p. 637.
and Artembares, fighting from a horse
very fit for understanding and discerning, as one who is skilled in the art of judging the age of horses.
I have a heart skilled in judging these things

where the second syllable is lengthened for the sake of the metre, as if it should be pronounced Ἱππομμέδοντος [Hippommedontos], which Priscian noted vol. 2 p. 415 ed. Krehl.: about which I have said more in my notes on Sophocles fr. 785 in the Oxford edition of 1860 p. 174 175.
the form of Hippomedon and his great bulk
they led under the chariot the horses that love the rein
the horse, as if panting through the bit, waits
and he whirls the horses, snorting in their headstalls
some on horses, others on ships
the Argive monster, the young of a horse
just as with horses I turn the rein beyond the course
and horses were entangled with horses
immortal skin and the toil of horses
